title: Sabres hire Milan Lucic as pro scout among series of hockey operations moves
content:
BUFFALO, N.Y. — The Buffalo Sabres announced a series of hires and promotions in their hockey department, one of which was hiring former Boston Bruins forward Milan Lucic as a pro scout.

Lucic retired this month after not having played in the NHL since the 2023-24 season. He played last season in Scotland and played five games for the Springfield Thunderbirds in the St. Louis Blues organization after joining the Blues in October on a professional tryout. He required reinstatement into the league after he was arrested and charged with assault and battery following an alleged domestic dispute in November 2023 and spent time in the NHL/NHLPA Player Assistance program. Prosecutors eventually dropped the charges after Lucic’s wife, Brittany, invoked marital privilege and chose not to testify against her husband.

Lucic wasn’t popular among Sabres fans during his Bruins career thanks to one memorable incident: In November 2011, he ran into Sabres goalie Ryan Miller after Miller came out of the net to play a loose puck. Miller wasn’t shy about expressing how he felt about the hit.

“I just stuck around because I just wanted to say what a piece of s— I think Lucic is,” Miller told reporters after the game. “Fifty pounds on me and runs me like that? It’s unbelievable. Everyone sees him as a big, tough, solid player. I respected him for how hard he plays. That was gutless. Gutless. Piece of s—.”

Lucic played more than 1,100 NHL games with the Bruins, Edmonton Oilers, Los Angeles Kings and Calgary Flames and finished his career with 586 points. This is his first job in hockey since his playing career ended.

Jarmo Kekäläinen took over as Sabres general manager in December and is starting to round out the hockey department in his image. In addition to hiring Lucic, Kekäläinen promoted Stacy Roest to director of player personnel and Rochester Americans general manager. Roest came to the Sabres midseason as a pro scout after more than a decade in the Tampa Bay Lightning organization. He was an assistant general manager in charge of player development and general manager of Tampa’s AHL team, the Syracuse Crunch.

Kekäläinen also promoted Tim Kennedy to director of player development. The role was vacant after the Sabres fired Adam Mair following his arrest for allegedly driving while intoxicated in September. Kennedy, a Buffalo native and former Sabre, has been working for the team as a development coach since 2021.

The Sabres also added Neil Komadoski as assistant director of pro scouting, Derek Dorsett as a forward development coach and Jarkko Ruutu as a European development coach. Komadoski spent the past 16 seasons as a pro scout for the Vancouver Canucks. Dorsett, who played 10 seasons in the NHL, was previously a development coach for the Columbus Blue Jackets. Ruutu spent the past decade with the Blue Jackets, including nine seasons as a development coach.
